News.title: Tragedy as mum & her two young children drown in Spain after swimming in popular dam lake
News.content:
SWIMMING TRAGEDY Tragedy as mum & her two young children drown in Spain after swimming in popular dam lake

A MUM and her two children have died in a horror triple drowning at a popular swimming hotspot.

The woman, 29, and her kids aged 11 and three, were found dead in the Ezra River in Spain.



The exact spot of the tragedy was the Roncal dam – a beloved picnicking spot with trees and clear blue waters at the heart of the Pyrenees.

Paramedics and an air ambulance raced to the river after the alarm was raised at 4:39pm today.



They worked for over an hour to revive the family – but sadly all three were confirmed dead at the scene.

The Civil Guard are treating the deaths as accidental but have launched a probe to confirm there were no suspicious circumstances.

The identity of the mother and her children has not yet been made public.

They are understood to be from the Roncal Valley.

News.title: Beloved family pets left to rot on piles of bones, ash and carcasses in squalid animal cemetery as probe launched
News.content:
GRAVEYARD SHAME Beloved family pets left to rot on piles of bones, ash and carcasses in squalid animal cemetery as probe launched

FAMILY pets were allegedly left to rot on piles of bones and in spilt bags of animal remains as a probe is launched into “squalid” conditions at a pet cremation service.

Animal Funeral Services, at Litfield House Farm near Kington in Herefordshire, has been served with a stop notice after one witness visited and described the “smell of death”.



Jess Roberts, 30, put down her rescue dog Teddy after 10 years together and she became determined to find out what happened to him.

The local vet said his remains had been sent to Animal Funeral Services and the dog groomer decided to visit the property with a friend.



On the business’ website it advertises “a dignified farewell”.

But upon arrival the smell hit them “like a punch in the face”.



“The smell of death surrounded the whole property. It was the smell of rotting carcasses” she said.

Roberts, from Bridgnorth in Shropshire, said she saw areas of the property closed off with pallets chained together.



She also said she counted around 10 dogs around the farm, some of which were panting and seemed to be in poor living conditions.

The business is supposedly open 24 hours so Roberts and her friend started shouting for someone to tend to the animals, she said.

She continued: “We wanted to let the owners know the dogs were panting. Then I stumbled across the worst thing I have ever seen.”



Roberts said she discovered bags full of animal remains, some of them were even split open and “there were flies everywhere”.

“There were bags that were split, with animals coming out of them.”

She first thought the bags were clinical waste but when she looked back at photos she realised they contained carcasses.



“Ashes don’t bleed” she added.

Elsewhere, she described cats with matted fur playing in piles of ashes that had small pieces of bone in.

She felt “there was no respect” towards the animals.

In one reportedly unlocked white van she said she found bags labelled “individual cremation”.

“These bags had dogs in them” she said.



In one horrific image an animal’s head appeared to be protruding from a bag.

Roberts said much of the material was too graphic for her to keep on her phone.

After the harrowing visit she contacted local police, the RSPCA and Herefordshire Council. The RSPCA and the council both told her it was the other organisation’s responsibility.

West Mercia Police said officers would attend the property but after four hours, Roberts said no one arrived and she had to eventually go home.

She left determined to return: “I said: ‘I’m going back tomorrow, and I’m going to keep going back until I speak to this woman and find my dog’.”



The next day she went back to Animal Funeral Services with her husband and confronted the owners.

The situation quickly escalated and she was arrested on suspicion of assault and then bailed.

Roberts said she approached Michelle Jenkins – thought to be a friend of the owner Rachael Slaughter – and asked where Teddy was.

While her husband spoke to the two women, Roberts repeatedly asked them where her dog was.

She said Slaughter could not provide paperwork for Teddy and gave no answers about the conditions the animals were in.



Roberts also said she had concerns about the lack of barriers around the furnaces.

She continued: “Nosy children or teenagers could have gone straight up to it.”

On July 9 the business was issued with a stop order from the APHA meaning it is prohibited from the use of animal by-products while the investigation is in progress.

Herefordshire Council said it was working with the APHA alongside the RSPCA and other relevant agencies.

The RSPCA can only investigate the welfare of the living animals on the site while premises handling and incinerating animal by-products is overseen by the APHA.



The agency will likely examine what checks were performed before animals were sent to the property and how much the local vets knew about the conditions.

Roberts said: “‘I can’t believe it took one 30-year-old grieving woman to turn up and check,”

She added: “Where was the legislation? Where was the registration? Where was everybody?”

Jess said: “Teddy is my best friend, he got me through everything, he saw me become a wife, a mum and a business owner.

“Now I’ll never get him back.”



Herefordshire Council said in a statement: “We are working with the Animal and Plant Health Agency, the RSPCA and other relevant agencies as part of the ongoing investigations and will take appropriate action within the council’s responsibilities and powers.”

West Mercia Police said: “We received a call around 3.40pm on Wednesday 8 July with a report of an assault on Titley Station Road, Lyonshall.

“A 30-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of assault and is currently on bail.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

APHA and Animal Funeral Services have been contacted for comment.

News.title: Incredible moment ‘dust devil mini tornado’ whips through UK farm shop car park during 36C heatwave
News.content:
THIS is the incredible moment a swirling “dust devil” mini tornado whipped through a farm shop car park as a heatwave baked the country.

Dramatic footage shows the spinning column of dust suddenly twisting into the sky before growing taller as stunned shoppers and staff look on.



The rare weather phenomenon can be seen swirling across the car park outside The Vine Farm Shop & Cafe in Spalding, Lincolnshire.

As the twister spins debris can be seen whipped up high into the air.



The unusual vortex was spotted as Britain continued to under soaring temperatures.

Staff at the farm shop watched in amazement as the towering spiral of dust formed before them.



The clip, captured last week, shows the striking spectacle as the column twists before gradually fading away.

A spokesperson for The Vine Farm Shop & Cafe said: “Not something we see every day in the Farm Shop & Cafe car park.”



The Met Office says dust devils are upward-spiralling vortices that can range from just a few feet high to more than 1,000ft.

Most dust devils are only a few metres wide at the base.

They typically last just a few minutes before cooler air cuts off their heat source.

Dust devils usually form during hot, dry weather when intense heating of the ground creates powerful updraughts.

It is the updraughts that lift dust and loose debris into the air.



Lincolnshire in the height of the heatwave experienced temperatures in the mid 30C’s.

The sighting came as the Met Office confirmed high pressure remains firmly in control of the UK’s weather, extending the current heatwave.

Forecasters say temperatures are expected to remain above average into late July.

They predict further hot spells possible into August.

They add there is also the chance of isolated showers and thunderstorms later this month.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The forecast also suggests that between late July and mid-August, we’re likely to see drier, brighter interludes.

The Met adds that the drier and brighter spells will be strongest across the south and southeast, with further hot spells possible.

News.title: Brits caught dropping a crisp packet face fines of up to £750 as ministers launch crackdown on litter-strewn streets
News.content:
PACK IT IN Brits caught dropping a crisp packet face fines of up to £750 as ministers launch crackdown on litter-strewn streets

BRITS caught dropping a crisp packet face fines of up to £750 as ministers launch a crackdown on Britain’s litter-strewn streets.

The maximum penalty for littering is being hiked by 50 per cent, while fly-tippers will be clobbered with fines of up to £5,000 – five times the current limit.



The tougher penalties will come into force this summer as part of a zero-tolerance crackdown on waste crime.

It is understood Labour wants to take a leaf out of Japan’s book, where littering is socially unacceptable and people routinely take their rubbish home.



Environment Secretary Emma Reynolds said: “Fly-tipping and littering is a disgrace that blights local communities.

“Under this government, criminals who break the rules will face heftier fines to clean up the mess they make.

“We are sending a clear message to those who dump their rubbish – we are coming after you and you will pay the price.”

Councils will be handed the power to issue the higher on-the-spot fines, with the amount depending on the seriousness of the offence.

The clampdown forms part of its wider Waste Crime Action Plan aimed at driving rogue waste operators out of business.

Ministers have already launched a new digital waste tracking system to better monitor rubbish from collection to disposal.



They have also tightened the rules so convicted fly-tippers can lose their waste licences under tougher court powers.

Advanced background checks have also been introduced to stop rogue operators setting up illegal waste businesses.

Councils have also been issued with fresh guidance on seizing vehicles used for fly-tipping and bringing offenders before the courts.

Chair of LGA Neighbourhoods Committee Cllr Arooj Shah said: “Increasing the maximum fixed penalty notices available to councils is a positive step and will give local authorities greater flexibility to tackle littering and fly-tipping in their communities.

“However, this should be accompanied by a review of sentencing guidelines. Our analysis has shown that the average court fine for fly-tipping remains lower than the average fixed penalty notice, undermining efforts to deter offenders.



“Stronger and more consistent penalties through the courts are needed to send a clear message that waste crime will not be tolerated.”

News.title: Teenager ‘sexually assaulted’ on popular trail in seaside town as cops say ‘attacker’ fled on e-scooter
News.content:

HORROR 'ATTACK' Teenager ‘sexually assaulted’ on popular trail in seaside town as cops say ‘attacker’ fled on e-scooter

A TEENAGE girl has allegedly been sexually assaulted on a popular trail in Skegness – with the suspect reportedly fleeing on a scooter.

Police received reports of a 16-year-old child being attacked by a man at around 8:30pm on Tuesday near King George’s Walk.



A drone and swarms of officers rushed to the scene to investigate the area.

The suspect has been described as stocky, about 5ft 5 inches tall, and with blond hair.



He is thought to be about 25 years old and was wearing a grey tracksuit top or hoodie at the time of the alleged attack.

According to witnesses, the man fled on an electric scooter from Burgh Road.



The suspect then went on to King George’s Walk from there, police claim.

Lincolnshire Police have issued an urgent appeal to hunt for the “attacker”.

News.title: Burnham reveals how he will deal with Trump after special relationship rift & Don said PM-to-be was ‘extremely liberal’
News.content:
ANDY'S TIGHTROPE Burnham reveals how he will deal with Trump after special relationship rift & Don said PM-to-be was ‘extremely liberal’

ANDY Burnham has revealed how he plans to deal with Donald Trump after the US president branded him “extremely liberal”.

The special relationship has been shaky in the final months of Sir Keir Starmer‘s tenure, with the two leaders locking horns over the Iran war.



But the former Greater Manchester mayor appeared optimistic about being able to handle Trump.

Speaking on Gary Lineker‘s podcast, Burnham said: “I’ll just meet him where he’s at.



“I like to think I’ve got some personality myself and I’ll deal with him very upfront in the same way. I think he likes people to deal with him.”

Burnham said that Trump’s recent description of him as “a mayor of a town” may have ruffled some feathers.

“He described Manchester as some town when he was referring to my position,” he said.

“You know what Mancs are like, Gary, that won’t have gone down fantastically well in the city I used to represent.”

He added: “But it’s about being yourself, isn’t it? It’s about respecting the office, the UK-US relationship.

“But where you disagree, do it in a way that is kind of meeting him where he’s at.”



It comes several weeks after Trump’s first comments on the PM-in-waiting.

After referring to him as “extremely liberal”, the president urged Burnham to follow a different energy policy to Starmer.

Trump suggested the former Manchester mayor should start taking oil from the North Sea if he becomes the next Labour leader.



He then slammed Sir Keir once again over Britain’s response to the Iran war.

Trump’s comments followed a series of swipes at Sir Keir over his refusal to open up the North Sea and his decision to instead greenlight more wind turbines.

He has blasted the outgoing PM on several occasions over the last two years, at one point calling him “no Churchill” for his inaction in the Middle East.

Asked about what he thought of Mr Burnham, the US leader said he thought the frontrunner for No10 was very left-wing and progressive.

Mr Trump said: “I don’t know, I think I see that he was, I guess, the mayor of a town.



“I hear he’s extremely liberal, extremely, so that means he probably won’t open up the North Sea.”

He added: “I gave Keir Starmer some pretty good advice. I said, open up the North Sea, go to Aberdeen, which was the hottest city of the whole continent.

“It was the oil city of Europe, and they closed everything. It was terrible. I couldn’t believe it.”

“The North Sea is loaded, I have had every oil company come to see me ‘Sir, could you give us access to the UK? We would do anything to drill in the North Sea’.

“The amazing thing is, they buy their oil from Norway, which gets the oil from the North Sea. Think of it, and they pay a big premium.



“Norway’s got now two trillion dollars in the bank, and the UK is dying, so they should open up the North Sea, and it’s an easy one, and a lot of good things are going to happen.

“It’s among the greatest deals in the world.”

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch warned that Britain was heading for a “summer of chaos” with Labour “obsessing about who they can tax to pay for more benefits” following Burnham’s interview.

“Andy Burnham isn’t even prime minister yet but he’s already talking about raising your taxes AGAIN,” she wrote on social media.

“We are heading for another summer of chaos with Labour obsessing about who they can tax to pay for more benefits.



“It doesn’t matter who is in charge, the problem is the Labour Party.”

News.title: Shock moment postie in England shirt ‘toe-punts’ blind Shih Tzu Ethel ‘like a football’ before pet tragically dies
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a postie wearing an England shirt “toe-punted” a blind Shih Tzu “like a football” before the pet tragically died.

Owner Eve Lewis, 40, wept as she spoke of her beloved pooch Ethel in the wake of the vile attack – who died from organ failure on Sunday.



The previous day, an unidentified parcel delivery man booted the 11-year-old Shih Tzu at the front door in Aylesbury, Bucks, leaving her with fatal injuries.

Eve said the Royal Mail postman denied kicking the small pup after handing her a parcel at around 11am on Saturday.



But her Ring Doorbell footage shows the man, dressed in an England football shirt, hoofing Ethel so she flew through the air and rolled along the ground.

She told The Sun that the incident was particularly shocking as her dog was partially blind and only had one tooth, and therefore posed no threat to the worker.

Eve said: “He didn’t even just kick her, he toe punted her like she was a football.

“She flew up in the air and hit the ground and rolled three times. She went flying like she was a football.



“The thing is, the driver was walking away and still made the effort to turn around and kick her.”

“I just don’t want this to happen to anyone else. I’m heartbroken and angry.

“I’ve gone through about 100 packs of tissues.



“When the kids went to school and my partner went to work this morning there was just silence.”

It is understood the postman, whom Eve did not recognise, has been suspended by the Royal Mail as police investigate.

The NHS worker, who lives with her 5-year-old son along with their only surviving dog – Stanley, a three-year-old French bulldog – described the frantic moments after the attack.

She took Ethel to the vets’, who could not save her. They concluded that she died from organ failure caused by blunt force trauma.

Eve added: “Her blood pressure dropped and they put tubes up her nose. Then they said there’s internal bleeding.



“At this point, I’m thinking, ‘This literally can’t be happening.’

“From then on, it was just a complete blur.”

“I went home overnight, but when I came back to the vets’ in the morning, she was pretty much already out of it.”

“We always called her Ethel 2.0 because after every surgery she had she would bounce back, but she didn’t make it this time. She was an old gal.”

Eve made the decision to put Ethel down when her vets told her the dog had suffered irreversible brain damage.



A Royal Mail spokesperson said: “We are deeply sorry for this distressing incident, and we know how upsetting it is for the family.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We are treating this matter very seriously. We have seen the footage and launched a full investigation to establish the circumstances. We have also confirmed to the family that we will cover the veterinary costs.

“We take animal welfare and the safety of our people very seriously. Dog-related incidents can present a serious risk to postal workers, and we will take any appropriate action once our investigation is complete.”

News.title: Family of Ann Widdecombe ‘terror murder’ suspect claim he had ‘no red flags’ but ‘spiralled’ after death of his dad
News.content:
THE FAMILY of Ann Widdecombe’s murder suspect were reeling from his arrest last night – and insisted: “We just cannot think why anybody would do this.”

His stunned uncle branded Ann’s killing “a terrible tragedy” and paid tribute to the 78-year-old veteran politician for her “strident and principled” beliefs.



The accused’s relative, 73, who we are not naming for legal reasons, told The Sun: “I liked Ann because she was forthright.

“She called a spade a spade. She was strident and principled and that’s why people were so fond of her.



“Never in a million years did I think he would be linked to this.

“I’m just absolutely flabbergasted. I was in total shock when I found out about his arrest, but now I’m just numb.”



Armed cops swooped on the 28-year-old reclusive loner at his home in Rotherham, South Yorkshire, on Saturday night shortly after 9pm.

CCTV obtained by The Sun showed him leaving the address five hours before Ann is believed to have been battered to death at her home 270 miles away in Devon.



A pole described by neighbours as “a wooden baton” could be seen sticking out of the pocket of his cargo shorts.

He was caught on CCTV returning to the red-brick council house at 6pm that evening and is believed to have completed a 540-mile round trip to carry out the “targeted attack”.

Counter-terror cops have since taken overall charge of the investigation after his home and devices were forensically searched amid a growing belief Ann’s killing was politically motivated.

He was arrested on suspicion of her murder and later re-arrested for the commission, preparation and commission of a terrorist act.

His uncle said he was one of three boys and lived at the property where he was arrested for most of his life.



His parents, who never married, split up over 15 years ago.

But whilst his teaching assistant mum moved out of the area to wed a new partner, his dad remained in the family home.

His older brother later joined the Armed Forces and moved to the south west whilst his younger sibling bought a house with his girlfriend.



But in December last year he was living alone after his amputee dad died of cancer.

His uncle described the prime suspect as “a gentle giant” – adding: “There have been no red flags at all.

“The only thing I can think of is is he’s been left on his own after his dad’s death and he’s spiralled.

“He’s always been a quiet, polite lad, and very shy.

“His two brothers would be rolling around play-fighting but he wouldn’t take part.



“He would sit at the side or move to the back.

“I had no idea what had happened until I saw the police tape around the house. It floored me when I found out.

“I just couldn’t believe it.”



Locals on the estate in Rotherham were also at a loss to explain his involvement in the killing of the former Tory turned Reform UK politician.

They described him as “a loner” and “a weirdo” who was rarely ever seen out.

One said: “He was a recluse. I’ve known him ever since he was a child. He used to come to ours for tea.

“He’s painfully shy. Even back then he liked to stay in his bedroom.

“His Dad did everything for him. But seriously, I cannot tell you the last time I saw him. I didn’t even know he lived there.



“There was even mould over the car. That should give you an idea of how little he went out.

“He was just quiet. Very, very quiet.”

Another neighbour said: “Everybody thought that he was a weirdo.



“He never left the house. He didn’t go out.

“On this estate, everybody knows everybody.

“It doesn’t matter who you are, whether you’re a quiet recluse or whatever, everybody knows everybody.

“But nobody’s seen or heard of him.”

Another said: “I’ve lived here five years and only ever seen him once.”



The UK’s most senior counter-terror cop said there was evidence of “planning” behind the attack on Ann.

But Met Police Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terror Policing, said officers were still working to understand the motive.

Officers potentially have up to two weeks to hold the suspect in custody before charging or releasing him.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They are continuing to pursue “multiple lines of inquiry”.

Devon and Cornwall Police have defended their handling of the investigation after repeatedly insisting that there was no evidence it was politically motivated.

News.title: Man 'brutally punched seagull' in front of kids after it tried to steal his food
News.content:
Man 'brutally punched seagull' in front of kids after it tried to steal his food

Police are investigating after a man allegedly grabbed a seagull by the harbour in Porthleven, Cornwall and 'smashed' it against a wall because it tried to steal his food

View Image A seagull was allegedly attacked for trying to steal food (stock) (Image: Ian Cooper/North Wales Live)

Police are investigating after a man 'grabbed and punched' a seagull in front of traumatised children at a seaside town, allegedly leaving it with broken wings.

‌



Devon and Cornwall Police said the incident took place by the harbour in Porthleven, Cornwall on Monday afternoon, with an onlooker claiming the it happened because the bird tried to steal food.

‌



A witness on social media alleged the man attacked the seagull at the Harbour View Café when it attempted to take his food and he then "stuffed it through a fence" - where it was left with broken wings.

‌



"This man brutally and repeatedly smashed a seagull against the wall of the Harbour View Café because it tried to steal some food," said the person, who added that there were shocked children watching on.

Ryanair issues airport delay warning to UK families over 15 destinations – list READ MORE :

"He then stuffed the seagull through the fence onto the road, where it floundered with two broken wings. This was in front of numerous people and children who were hugely upset."

‌



Police are now appealing for anyone with relevant footage or information to come forward, reports CornwallLive.

A spokesperson for Devon and Cornwall Police said: "We have been made aware following a report of a seagull being injured by a man by the harbour in Porthleven on the afternoon of Monday, July 13.

"It was reported the suspect grabbed and punched the seagull leaving it injured. Enquiries into the matter are ongoing. Anybody with any relevant footage or information is asked to call 101 or visit our website quoting 50260183379."

Article continues below

Seagulls are protected by law as are all wild birds.

The RSPCA states on its website: "Like all wild birds, gulls, their chicks and their nests are protected under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981. This means it's illegal to intentionally kill, take or injure gulls, take or destroy their eggs, or damage or destroy any gull nests while they're in use or being built - unless you're acting under licence.

"Although gulls are a common sight in many areas near the coast, some species of gull, such as herring gulls and kittiwakes, are actually on the UK Red List. They're considered species of conservation concern in the UK because there's evidence suggesting that their populations are in decline overall."

News.title: Tom Kerridge shares Italian recipes and praises Andy Burnham's plans for hospitality
News.content:
Speaking ahead of the launch tonight of his new ITV show, Tom Kerridge Cooks Italy, top chef Tom Kerridge tells The Mirror: “When hospitality grows, the rest of the country grows. And Andy Burnham understands that.” It comes as Britain’s next Prime Minister calls for VAT in the sector to be slashed from 20% to 10%.

Owner with his wife, sculptor Beth Cullen-Kerridge, of The Hand and Flowers, near his home in Marlow, Buckinghamshire, it became the first and only pub to be awarded two coveted Michelin stars in 2006 and 2012. Tom, 52, who shares a son, Acey, 10, with Beth, says: “Hospitality needs to be backed and Andy Burnham is the man for the job.”

A lifelong Labour supporter, he adds: “I grew up in a single parent family on an estate in Gloucester. Labour represents a workforce, it tries to ensure that people have an opportunity regardless of background. If you come from a background that is economically struggling I think there should be systems in place: quality transport systems that allow you to get to work; a healthcare system that works.

View 9 Images Tom Kerridge is calling for VAT to be slashed from 20% to 10% "in line with the rest of Europe" (Image: Jam Press)

‌



“Irrespective if you grew up on an estate or a semi detached house, I think everyone should be presented with opportunities. The party that offers that has always been the Labour party.”

Burnham has proved himself in Manchester, says Tom, who ran popular eatery The Bull and Bear in the city from 2019 to 2022. He says: “Manchester is one of the most forward thinking, eclectic cities and that is something he has been a part of, keeping the cogs moving for reinvestment.

“Hospitality is at the base level of everything, exciting restaurants, great hotels, late night spaces. Manchester has all this energy that has been able to drive forward and allow investment and therefore other business to thrive too - property investment, tech companies, multimedia spaces.

“Manchester has a beating heart that comes from people hanging out together in hospitality. The rest of the country hasn't quite got that yet. What we want is the Andy Burnham approach.”

‌



View 9 Images When it comes to saving hospitality, Tom says: "Andy Burnham is the man for the job." (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Chef and publican Tom has spearheaded the #VATsTheProblem movement, gathering more than 250,000 signatures on a petition calling for a fairer 10% VAT rate for hospitality.

During his Makerfield campaign, Andy Burnham pledged to bring hospitality VAT down to 10%, to slash business rates for puns by 20% and to review cost pressures like National Insurance contributions. Tom says: “From my conversation with Andy I think he really understands.”

With industry sources saying one in six hospitality businesses are at risk of closure in the next year, Tom continues: “Things are shutting because of ongoing costs that have dropped in over many years of neglect of the industry: food inflation, energy bills, National Insurance increases.

‌



“On top of that, we have the second highest tax in Europe at 20%. Norway is 21%, everyone else is at between 8-12%. Ireland is dropping down to 9%. What we're asking for is to sit the same as Europe

View 9 Images Tom Kerridge and his wife, Beth Cullen-Kerridge (Image: Getty Images)

“We want growth, reinvestment, reemployment. If the Government could just get out of the way and let us operate, we are the beating heart of the reinvestment of the rest of the country.”

A familiar figure on our TV screens, Tom’s credits include Great British Menu, Saturday Kitchen, MasterChef, and he’s presented series including Tom Kerridge’s Proper Pub Food. And when he is not working, he is determined to use his fame to fight for the industry he loves.

‌



One nation that really knows how to do hospitality, according to Tom, is Italy, and he is great lover of Italian cuisine. Ahead of Tom Cooks Italy, he says: “Italian recipes are a celebration of ingredients and relatively simple. You don't need to be a super confident cook to try them or prepare for four days.

View 9 Images Tom says: "The Italian lifestyle is all based on food, restaurant, community, connection."

“I'm hooked on all things Italy after visiting. I've been back twice since we finished filming. I took the family to Pompeii then to see Napoli vs AC Milan, then to the Colosseum.”

Of Italians and their cuisine, he says: “They celebrate their produce, their culture, where it comes from - olive oil in Tuscany, for example. The lifestyle is all based on food, restaurant, community, connection. We should use Italy as an example of how we should do things.”

‌



And the passionate chef, who has shared a delicious Italian recipe with Mirror readers, remains optimistic about the future of British fare, too. He says: “Fingers crossed Andy Burnham brings in new energy. Andy Burnham is the man we need.”

*Tom Kerridge Cooks Italy, starts Thurs 16th July, 7.30pm on ITV1 and ITVX, proudly supported by M&S

Calabrian chilli, sausage and butterbean stew

View 9 Images Calabrian chilli, sausage and butterbean stew (Image: South Shore/ITV)

‌



Serves 4

2 tbsp olive oil

500g Italian style pork and fennel sausages

4 M&S Collection Master Grill Spicy Calabrian sausages, halved lengthways and sliced

2 onions, finely diced

4 cloves garlic, finely chopped

1 tsp fennel seeds

1 heaped tbsp tomato puree

2 Calabrian chillies, sliced

3 tbsp M&S Hot Calabrian chilli paste

200ml white wine

400ml chicken stock

4 sprigs fresh oregano, leaves picked

2 sprigs rosemary, finely chopped

2 cans chopped tomatoes

2 cans butterbeans, drained

2 tbsp flat leaf parsley, roughly chopped

For the garlic and chilli ciabatta

1 M&S ciabatta loaf

100g softened butter

1 tbsp M&S Hot Calabrian chilli paste

1 clove garlic, finely grated

‌



View 9 Images Calabrian chilli, sausage and butterbean stew (Image: Tom Regester/South Shore/ITV)

Method

Preheat oven to 180C fan Heat the oil in a large sauté pan. When hot, add the Italian style sausages and cook them until lightly browned on each side. Remove and place them onto a tray. Place the tray into the oven for 15-20 minutes. Next add the spicy Calabrian sausages to the pan and cook for 3-4 minutes. Add the onions to the pan and sautè for 5 minutes. Next add the garlic and stir gently for 2 more minutes. Add the fennel seeds and stir well. Pop in the tomato puree and chillies and stir again for another couple of minutes. Pour in the wine and let it reduce by half. Add in the stock and let that reduce by half. Add the tomatoes and bring up to a gentle simmer. Reduce the heat, add the beans and herbs, cook for 15-20 minutes on low. Remove the sausages from the oven and let them rest for a few minutes. While the stew is cooking, mix the ingredients for the chilli butter together and season with a little salt. Halve the ciabatta lengthways and lay this onto a tray cut side up. Spread liberally with the chilli butter. Pop into the preheated oven and cook for 15 minutes or until golden and crunchy. Thickly slice the sausages and pop them into the stew. Finish with lots of fresh parsley and season with salt and pepper. Remove the bread from the oven and cut into thick pieces. Serve the sausage and butterbean stew into bowls with the chilli bread alongside.
